 No dedicated discussions of the text were retrieved in the examined secondary literature.

According to computational text analysis by DharmaNexus, the text exhibits 53 instances of Pali-internal reuse across 14 texts [DharmaNexus]. Its primary textual partner is the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (Paṭhamo bhāgo), which contains 26 shared passages (totalling 2,093 characters) and exhibits substantial textual overlap with the apadāna's opening and central portions (§0.3–5.4) [DharmaNexus]. The poem also shares recurring poetic and narrative formulas—especially across segments §4–8—with numerous other apadāna texts, most substantially the *Atthasandassakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 139), *Tikicchakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 181), *Tilamuṭṭhidāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 274), and *Ñāṇasaññikattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 130) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matching, DharmaNexus identifies a low-plausibility alignment (score 25) with the Tibetan version of the *Samādhirājasūtra* (D0127) at segment §1.2, which represents incidental phraseological similarity rather than a confirmed historical parallel [DharmaNexus].
